title: Compounding of offences - which cases can genuinely be settled
p1:
Not every criminal case has to end with a long courtroom battle.

But here is the surprising part: not every dispute can simply be settled because both sides agree.
p2:
Many people believe that if a complainant and accused reach a compromise, the case automatically ends. That is not true.

Compounding of offences means certain offences can be legally settled by the parties, but only those specifically allowed by law. The purpose is to resolve minor disputes without unnecessary litigation while keeping serious offences outside private settlements.
p3:
For example, some offences involving personal disputes, minor harm, or property-related conflicts may be compoundable. However, crimes affecting society at large usually cannot be closed just because the parties want a settlement.

The key lesson: a compromise between two people and a legally valid compounding of an offence are not always the same thing.
conclusion: Should more offences be allowed to be settled privately, or should the law keep stricter limits to protect public interest?
